data.definition: In a suitable state for an activity or event.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'ready for' before nouns/events. Use 'ready to' before base verbs (ready to go).
examples: Are you ready for dinner?
The team is ready for the final match.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We are ready to the test. ➜ ✅ We are ready for the test.

data.definition: Closely connected or appropriate to what is being done or considered.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'relevant'. Never use 'for' or 'with'.
examples: Please submit documents relevant to your visa application.
His remarks were not relevant to the discussion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The experience is relevant for the job. ➜ ✅ The experience is relevant to the job.

data.definition: Dependent on someone or something for survival, support, or success.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'reliant on' or 'reliant upon'.
examples: The business is heavily reliant on international clients.
Hospitals are reliant on backup generators.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We are reliant from solar power. ➜ ✅ We are reliant on solar power.

data.definition: Dependent on someone or something with high reliance.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'reliant upon' (more formal) or 'reliant on'.
examples: Modern agriculture is reliant upon automated machinery.
She is reliant upon her family for emotional support.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is reliant to public transport. ➜ ✅ He is reliant upon public transport.

data.pattern: be + reluctant about + [something] / reluctant to + [do something]
data.definition: Unwilling and hesitant to take an action.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'reluctant about' before nouns/topics. Use 'reluctant to' before base verbs (reluctant to go).
examples: She felt reluctant about moving to a new city.
He was reluctant to sign the agreement.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is reluctant for changing jobs. ➜ ✅ He is reluctant about changing jobs.

data.pattern: be + reminiscent of + [past era / person / place]
data.definition: Tending to remind one of something or someone.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'reminiscent'.
examples: The architecture in New Orleans is reminiscent of French colonial style.
Her tone was reminiscent of her mother's.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The melody is reminiscent about old jazz. ➜ ✅ The melody is reminiscent of old jazz.

data.definition: Typical of a class, group, or body of opinion.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'representative'.
examples: The survey sample was representative of the national demographic.
His opinion is representative of the whole committee.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The sample is representative for voters. ➜ ✅ The sample is representative of voters.

data.definition: Feeling or expressing bitterness or indignation at having been treated unfairly.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'resentful of' a person or advantage, or 'resentful about' an action.
examples: He was deeply resentful of his boss's favoritism.
She felt resentful about being passed over for promotion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She was resentful for the decision. ➜ ✅ She was resentful of the decision.

data.definition: Having control over or duty for someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'for' after 'responsible' when stating duties. Do NOT use 'to' directly before a noun duty.
examples: Who is responsible for managing the event budget?
She is responsible for training new employees.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She is responsible to supervise the team. ➜ ✅ She is responsible for supervising the team.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Adjective: 'responsible for' ➔ Related Noun: 'take responsibility for'

data.definition: Correct in one's opinion or statement.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'right about' when confirming accuracy of an opinion or fact.
examples: You were totally right about that restaurant; the food was great!
She was right about the meeting time.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is right on the facts. ➜ ✅ He is right about the facts.

data.definition: Lacking manners or respect; offensive toward someone.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'rude' when directed at a recipient.
examples: It is wrong to be rude to waiters.
She was angry because he was rude to her.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Don't be rude with him. ➜ ✅ Don't be rude to him.

data.definition: An action performed or feeling experienced in response to a situation or event.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'reaction' to identify the stimulus.
examples: What was his initial reaction to the proposal?
She suffered an allergic reaction to the medication.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Her reaction for the movie was unexpected. ➜ ✅ Her reaction to the movie was unexpected.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reaction TO the news' ➔ Verb: 'react to'

data.definition: A cause, explanation, or justification for an event or action.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'reason FOR' + noun/gerund. Contrast with the conjunction phrase 'because OF'.
examples: What was the main reason for his absence yesterday?
She explained her reason for resigning.
data.common_mistake: ❌ What was the reason of his anger? ➜ ✅ What was the reason for his anger?
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reason for the delay' ➔ Conjunction: 'delayed because of the rain'

data.definition: The way in which two or more people or things are connected.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'relationship WITH' a person, and 'relationship BETWEEN' two entities.
examples: She has a wonderful relationship with her mother.
We need to examine the relationship between diet and health.
data.common_mistake: ❌ What is your relationship to him? ➜ ✅ What is your relationship with him?

data.definition: The quality or state of being closely connected or appropriate.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'relevant to'. Always use 'relevance TO'.
examples: The judge questioned the relevance of the evidence to the trial.
His experience has direct relevance to this role.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Relevance for the topic. ➜ ✅ Relevance to the topic.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'relevance TO the debate' ➔ Adjective: 'relevant to'

data.definition: Dependence on or trust in someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'rely on' and adjective 'reliant on'.
examples: Heavy reliance on automated tools can lead to skill loss.
Their reliance on seasonal labor caused problems.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Reliance to imports. ➜ ✅ Reliance on imports.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'reliance ON public transit' ➔ Verb: 'rely on' ➔ Adjective: 'reliant on'

data.definition: The beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'reputation FOR' a characteristic. Contrast with adjective 'famous for'.
examples: The university has an international reputation for research excellence.
He has a reputation for being punctual.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A reputation of honesty. ➜ ✅ A reputation for honesty.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a reputation FOR reliability' ➔ Adjective: 'famous for'

data.definition: An act of asking politely or formally for something.
data.grammar_rule: The noun 'request FOR' takes 'for'. Contrast with the verb 'request' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: Management approved her request for extra funding.
Send your request for information via email.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He made a request of help. ➜ ✅ He made a request for help.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'a request FOR assistance' ➔ Verb: 'request' (no prep)

data.definition: Systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'research INTO' or 'research ON'.
examples: Scientific research into cancer treatments receives high funding.
She is doing research on medieval history.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Research about cancer. ➜ ✅ Research into cancer.

data.definition: The refusal to accept or comply with something; the ability not to be affected by something.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'resistant to'. Always use 'resistance TO'.
examples: There was strong public resistance to the new tax law.
Bacteria can develop resistance to antibiotics.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Resistance against change. ➜ ✅ Resistance to change.

data.definition: A feeling of deep admiration for someone or something elicited by their abilities or qualities.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'respect FOR' people or rules. Contrast with adjective 'respectful to'.
examples: Children should learn respect for others.
He showed great respect for his elders.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Show respect to the rules. ➜ ✅ Show respect for the rules.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'respect FOR the law' ➔ Adjective: 'respectful to'

data.definition: A verbal or written answer, or a reaction to something.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'response'.
examples: We received a swift response to our complaint letter.
In response to customer feedback, we changed the menu.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Here is my response for your question. ➜ ✅ Here is my response to your question.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'response TO our email' ➔ Verb: 'answer' (no prep)

data.definition: The state or fact of having a duty to deal with something or having control over someone.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'responsible for'. Use 'responsibility FOR' a duty.
examples: He accepted full responsibility for the accident.
Managing safety is the responsibility of the supervisor.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Responsibility to manage the team. ➜ ✅ Responsibility for managing the team.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'take responsibility FOR the error' ➔ Adjective: 'responsible for'

data.definition: A limiting condition or measure.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'restriction ON'.
examples: The government lifted restrictions on international travel.
Imposing restrictions on free speech is dangerous.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Restrictions for imports. ➜ ✅ Restrictions on imports.

data.definition: A consequence, effect, or outcome of something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'result OF' as a noun. Contrast with verb 'result from'.
examples: The high test scores were the direct result of hard work.
He suffered injuries as a result of the collision.
data.common_mistake: ❌ As a result from the storm, power failed. ➜ ✅ As a result of the storm, power failed.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the result OF the study' ➔ Verb: 'result from'

data.definition: An increase in number, size, amount, or quality.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'IN' after 'rise' before the fluctuating noun.
examples: The rise in sea levels threatens coastal areas.
Employees welcomed the rise in minimum wage.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A rise of cost. ➜ ✅ A rise in cost.

data.definition: To arrive at or attain a place, goal, or stage.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'at' after 'reach'.
examples: We reached the hotel late in the evening.
The negotiators reached a final agreement after midnight.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We reached to London at 5 PM. ➔ ✅ We reached London at 5 PM.

data.definition: To look at and comprehend written text.
examples: He reads the newspaper every morning.
She read three books last month.
I have read that novel twice.

data.definition: To bind again or bounce back.
examples: Prices rebound after drop.
Stock market rebounded quickly today.
Economy has rebound from slump.

data.definition: To construct again after damage.
examples: City rebuilds after earthquake disaster.
They rebuilt bridge in six months.
Community has rebuilt homes.

data.definition: To reformulate arguments or roles.
examples: Philosopher recasts classic debate.
Author recast narrative structure.
Premise has been recast entirely.

data.definition: To identify from previous knowledge.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition.
examples: I recognized her instantly.
Do you recognize this song?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I recognize to her. ➔ ✅ I recognize her.

data.definition: To do something again.
examples: He redoes task until perfect.
She redid entire room interior decoration.
We have redone electrical wiring.

data.definition: To stop oneself from doing something or hold back voluntarily.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'from' + gerund (-ing).
examples: Please refrain from smoking inside the auditorium.
He refrained from making any further comments.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Please refrain to take photos. ➔ ✅ Please refrain from taking photos.

data.definition: To depend on or trust someone/something to work or act properly.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'on'. Followed by noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing).
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'rely on facts' ➔ Noun: 'place reliance ON data'
examples: You can always rely on her to deliver high-quality work on time.
Modern businesses rely heavily on cloud infrastructure.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Rely of public transport. ➔ ✅ Rely on public transport.

data.definition: To stay in the same place or condition.
data.grammar_rule: Formal synonym of stay; used with 'in' or 'at'.
examples: Please remain in your seats.
They remained at home.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Remain on your seats. ➔ ✅ Remain in your seats.

data.definition: To make again or differently.
examples: Studio remakes classic film version.
She remade dress for gala evening.
Song has been remade in acoustic.

data.definition: To bring to mind or retain in memory.
data.grammar_rule: Can take a direct object or 'about'.
examples: I remember your name.
Remember about the meeting.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I remember about your name. ➔ ✅ I remember your name.

data.definition: To fix or restore to good condition.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb.
examples: He repaired his bicycle.
Can you repair this car?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Repair to the bike. ➔ ✅ Repair the bike.

data.definition: To be directly responsible to a supervisor, or to provide an account of progress.
data.grammar_rule: Report TO + person (line manager/supervisor); report ON + subject/progress.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He reports to the head of marketing' ➔ Noun: 'Direct report TO the director'
examples: He reports to the head of marketing and works closely with his team.
The regional managers report directly to the CEO.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He reports at the manager. ➔ ✅ He reports to the manager.

data.definition: To ask for something politely or formally.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition. Noun 'request' takes 'for'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She requested assistance' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'A request FOR assistance' (uses FOR)
examples: Passengers are requested to remain seated.
I requested a copy of the official transcript.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I requested for a room upgrade. ➔ ✅ I requested a room upgrade.

data.definition: To sell again to another buyer.
examples: He resells vintage clothes online.
She resold concert tickets at cost.
Items have been resold at profit.

data.definition: To look like or be similar to another person or thing.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'with' after 'resemble'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She resembles her mother' ➔ Noun: 'She bears a resemblance TO her mother'
examples: The twins strongly resemble each other in appearance.
This new software resembles our old interface.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She resembles with her mother. ➔ ✅ She resembles her mother.

data.definition: To set again or restore default.
examples: System resets automatically overnight.
He reset router to restore connection.
Timer has been reset to zero.

data.definition: To formally give up one's job, office, or position.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive career verb requiring 'from' before the position relinquished.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Resign from post' ➔ Noun: 'Hand in resignation FROM post'
examples: The CEO resigned from his post amid public scrutiny.
She decided to resign from the board of directors.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He resigned of his job. ➔ ✅ He resigned from his job.

data.definition: To turn to a extreme or unpleasant strategy because no other options remain.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure. 'To' is a preposition, followed by noun or gerund.
examples: They had to resort to legal action to recover the money.
Never resort to violence to solve personal conflicts.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Resort into extreme measures. ➔ ✅ Resort to extreme measures.

data.definition: Having the duty to take care of someone or something, or being the cause of an outcome.
data.grammar_rule: Adjective phrase requiring FOR + noun or gerund (-ing). Do NOT use TO + verb infinitive directly after 'responsible for'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Adjective: 'responsible FOR overseeing' ➔ Noun: 'take responsibility FOR something'
examples: Sarah is responsible for overseeing the entire organization.
Who is responsible for managing customer feedback?
data.common_mistake: ❌ She is responsible to oversee the team. ➔ ✅ She is responsible for overseeing the team.

data.definition: To reconsider or think again.
examples: Company rethinks marketing strategy.
They rethought plans after review.
We have rethought our approach.

data.definition: To come or go back.
data.grammar_rule: Use to for destination and from for origin.
examples: He returned to his office.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Return in office. ➔ ✅ Return to his office.

data.definition: To wind back to beginning.
examples: He rewinds video cassette tape.
She rewound film to start scene.
Tape has been rewound completely.

data.definition: To write again or revise text.
examples: Author rewrites draft story chapter.
She rewrote essay to improve flow.
Article has been rewritten cleanly.

data.definition: To sit on and control a horse or bike.
examples: She rides her bike to work.
He rode a horse across the field.
They have ridden camels in Egypt.

data.definition: To make a clear resonant sound.
examples: The phone rings loudly in the hall.
He rang the doorbell twice.
The church bell has rung twelve times.

data.definition: To move upward or increase.
examples: The sun rises in the east.
Prices rose sharply last month.
The river level has risen by two feet.

data.definition: To move swiftly on foot.
examples: He runs five kilometers every morning.
She ran to catch the train.
They have run two marathons this year.

data.definition: To use up all of something so that none is left.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable 2-particle phrasal verb requiring 'of' before the exhausted supply.
examples: We ran out of milk this morning during breakfast.
Hurry up! We are running out of time.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We ran out from gas. ➔ ✅ We ran out of gas.
